question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose this generic external-verification approval API and persisted attempt/grant model in core, with verification-provider behavior remaining plugin-owned?
rationale: The RFC and tracker support a generic seam, but this PR creates broad stable SDK, protocol, client, and persistence contracts that cannot be safely accepted solely from contributor implementation evidence.

options.title: Sponsor the generic core seam
options.body: Confirm the host-owned API direction, then require a rebased branch and inspectable successful end-to-end proof before merging.

options.title: Narrow the core contract
options.body: Keep only the minimum missing plugin API in core and move reusable-grant or presentation-specific behavior into the owner plugin.

options.title: Defer the public API
options.body: Leave the tracker open until maintainers choose a stable approval and persistence contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the generic core seam
recommendation.body: Confirm the host-owned API direction, then require a rebased branch and inspectable successful end-to-end proof before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: The tracker identifies Kevin as the RFC acceptance contact for the product direction this PR implements.
